title: Hotel Price Tracker — input

hotelNames.title: Properties by name
hotelNames.description: Hotels by name, e.g. ["Hyatt Regency Lisbon", "Altis Grand Hotel Lisbon"]: use for "track the price of hotel X" when you have no Google Hotels URL. One free Google search per name; the listing is kept only when its name shares at least two words and 60% of the words you typed, so a stranger is never billed. A name that matches nothing is a free not_found status row: retry with the name as Google spells it, or pass the entity_id of any row in hotels. Add the city to a generic name.

hotels.title: Properties (Google Hotels URLs or entity tokens)
hotels.description: Exact hotels by Google Hotels URL (https://www.google.com/travel/hotels/entity/ChkI…) or entity token, e.g. the entity_id of a row from an earlier run or from kestrel/google-hotels-prices. No search: one offers call per hotel and date, nothing unrelated is ever billed. Use to track the SAME hotels every day: resolve names once, then pass their entity_id values here. Names belong in hotelNames.

checkIn.title: First check-in date
checkIn.description: First check-in date of the window: "2026-11-02" (YYYY-MM-DD), or relative to the day the run starts: "30 days", "6 weeks", "+30d", "today", "tomorrow". Use relative dates for a schedule ("track prices daily"): the input never needs editing and every run looks the same distance ahead. A past date is rejected before anything is charged. Required.

days.title: Check-in dates to cover
days.description: How many consecutive check-in dates to price from checkIn, 1 to 60, e.g. 30 (default 7). One row per hotel and date, so 2 hotels × days 30 = at most 60 rows ($0.24). 1 = one stay, 7 = a week, 30 = a month-long price calendar. Use for "which day is cheapest", "price calendar", "cheapest date to stay": rank_in_window ranks the dates and cheapest_in_window marks the winner. Each date is one offers call.

nights.title: Nights
nights.description: Length of stay in nights for every check-in date, 1 to 30, e.g. 2 (default 1). Check-out = check-in + nights: checkIn "2026-11-02", nights 2, days 3 = three 2-night stays checking in on 2, 3 and 4 Nov.

maxPrice.title: Only keep dates at or under this nightly rate
maxPrice.description: 0 (default) = deliver every date. N = deliver only the check-in dates whose lowest nightly rate is at or under N in `currency`, e.g. 180: the price drop alert. Dates over N are never billed; a run that delivers nothing means nothing is under target yet, and the status row still reports the cheapest rate and date it saw. rank_in_window is computed over the whole window before this filter. Use for "alert me when hotel X drops under 180", "only dates under budget".

adults.title: Adults
adults.description: Adults in the room, 1 to 6, e.g. 2 (default 2). Google prices ONE room for the whole party: there is no rooms input, and above 6 adults Google returns no price at all. Rates scale with occupancy exactly as on Google, so track the occupancy you will book.

childrenAges.title: Children (ages)
childrenAges.description: Ages of the children in the same room, e.g. [5, 9] for two children aged 5 and 9. Empty (default) = no children. The price is for one room holding the adults plus these children.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: ISO 4217 code for every price in the run, e.g. "EUR" (default "USD"): USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, THB, SGD, AUD, AED… When the user names no currency, pass the destination's ("EUR" for Lisbon). maxPrice is read in this currency.

country.title: Market
country.description: Google market (gl): any 2-letter country code, e.g. "gb", "pt", "jp" (default "us"). It is the country of the person booking, NOT the destination: keep "us" unless the user wants prices as seen from a country. It changes which booking sites Google lists (Klook, Traveloka, Wego in Asian markets), so keep one market across a price history.

language.title: Language
language.description: Google language (hl), e.g. "en", "de", "ja" (default "en"). Sets the language of hotel and source names where Google has a translation; hotelNames may be written in any language.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy
proxyConfiguration.description: Keep the default (Apify datacenter proxies): Google accepts them for these calls, residential is unnecessary.

sessions.title: Parallel proxy sessions
sessions.description: Parallel proxy sessions, 1 to 16, e.g. 4 (default 4); each is paced at perIp requests per second. Raise for many hotels × dates, lower if Google throttles.

perIp.title: Requests per second per IP
perIp.description: Requests per second per proxy session, 0.1 to 2, e.g. 0.5 (default 0.5). 0.5 is safe; raise carefully.

description: Hotel price tracker on Google Hotels. Minimal input: {"hotelNames": ["Hyatt Regency Lisbon"], "checkIn": "30 days", "days": 7}. One of hotelNames / hotels is required. days decides the bill: one row per hotel and check-in date at $0.004 (7 dates = $0.028 per hotel); maxPrice delivers and bills only the dates at or under your target.
